paragraphs.text: And the Pharisees and Sadducees came, and trying him asked him to show them a sign from heaven.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ Σαδδουκαῖοι πειράζοντες ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν σημεῖον ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐπιδεῖξαι αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: Kai proselthontes hoi Pharisaioi kai Saddoukaioi peirazontes epērōtēsan auton sēmeion ek tou ouranou epideixai autois.

paragraphs.text: But he answered and said unto them, When it is evening, ye say, [It will be] fair weather: for the heaven is red.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὀψίας γενομένης λέγετε· Εὐδία, πυρράζει γὰρ ὁ οὐρανός·
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen autois· Opsias genomenēs legete· Eudia, pyrrazei gar ho ouranos·

paragraphs.text: And in the morning, [It will be] foul weather to-day: for the heaven is red and lowering. Ye know how to discern the face of the heaven; but ye cannot [discern] the signs of the times.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πρωΐ· Σήμερον χειμών, πυρράζει γὰρ στυγνάζων ὁ οὐρανός. τὸ μὲν πρόσωπον τοῦ οὐρανοῦ γινώσκετε διακρίνειν, τὰ δὲ σημεῖα τῶν καιρῶν οὐ δύνασθε.
paragraphs.translit: kai prōi· Sēmeron cheimōn, pyrrazei gar stygnazōn ho ouranos. to men prosōpon tou ouranou ginōskete diakrinein, ta de sēmeia tōn kairōn ou dynasthe.

paragraphs.text: An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given unto it, but the sign of Jonah. And he left them, and departed.
paragraphs.original: Γενεὰ πονηρὰ καὶ μοιχαλὶς σημεῖον ἐπιζητεῖ, καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ τὸ σημεῖον Ἰωνᾶ. καὶ καταλιπὼν αὐτοὺς ἀπῆλθεν.
paragraphs.translit: Genea ponēra kai moichalis sēmeion epizētei, kai sēmeion ou dothēsetai autē ei mē to sēmeion Iōna. kai katalipōn autous apēlthen.

paragraphs.text: And the disciples came to the other side and forgot to take bread.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐλθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ εἰς τὸ πέραν ἐπελάθοντο ἄρτους λαβεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai elthontes hoi mathētai eis to peran epelathonto artous labein.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus said unto them, Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὁρᾶτε καὶ προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous eipen autois· Horate kai prosechete apo tēs zymēs tōn Pharisaiōn kai Saddoukaiōn.

paragraphs.text: And they reasoned among themselves, saying, We took no bread.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ διελογίζοντο ἐν ἑαυτοῖς λέγοντες ὅτι Ἄρτους οὐκ ἐλάβομεν.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de dielogizonto en heautois legontes hoti Artous ouk elabomen.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus perceiving it said, O ye of little faith, why reason ye among yourselves, because ye have no bread?
paragraphs.original: γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Τί διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, ὀλιγόπιστοι, ὅτι ἄρτους οὐκ ἐλάβετε;
paragraphs.translit: gnous de ho Iēsous eipen· Ti dialogizesthe en heautois, oligopistoi, hoti artous ouk elabete;

paragraphs.text: Do ye not yet perceive, neither remember the five loaves of the five thousand, and how many baskets ye took up?
paragraphs.original: οὔπω νοεῖτε, οὐδὲ μνημονεύετε τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους τῶν πεντακισχιλίων καὶ πόσους κοφίνους ἐλάβετε;
paragraphs.translit: oupō noeite, oude mnēmoneuete tous pente artous tōn pentakischiliōn kai posous kophinous elabete;

paragraphs.text: Neither the seven loaves of the four thousand, and how many baskets ye took up?
paragraphs.original: οὐδὲ τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἄρτους τῶν τετρακισχιλίων καὶ πόσας σπυρίδας ἐλάβετε;
paragraphs.translit: oude tous hepta artous tōn tetrakischiliōn kai posas spyridas elabete;

paragraphs.text: How is it that ye do not perceive that I spake not to you concerning bread? But beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
paragraphs.original: πῶς οὐ νοεῖτε ὅτι οὐ περὶ ἄρτων εἶπον ὑμῖν; προσέχετε δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων.
paragraphs.translit: pōs ou noeite hoti ou peri artōn eipon hymin; prosechete de apo tēs zymēs tōn Pharisaiōn kai Saddoukaiōn.

paragraphs.text: Then understood they that he bade them not beware of the leaven of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
paragraphs.original: τότε συνῆκαν ὅτι οὐκ εἶπεν προσέχειν ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν ἄρτων ἀλλὰ ἀπὸ τῆς διδαχῆς τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων.
paragraphs.translit: tote synēkan hoti ouk eipen prosechein apo tēs zymēs tōn artōn alla apo tēs didachēs tōn Pharisaiōn kai Saddoukaiōn.

paragraphs.text: Now when Jesus came into the parts of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, Who do men say that the Son of man is?
paragraphs.original: Ἐλθὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὰ μέρη Καισαρείας τῆς Φιλίππου ἠρώτα τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγων· Τίνα λέγουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι εἶναι τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου;
paragraphs.translit: Elthōn de ho Iēsous eis ta merē Kaisareias tēs Philippou ērōta tous mathētas autou legōn· Tina legousin hoi anthrōpoi einai ton hyion tou anthrōpou;

paragraphs.text: And they said, Some [say] John the Baptist; some, Elijah; and others, Jeremiah, or one of the prophets.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Οἱ μὲν Ἰωάννην τὸν βαπτιστήν, ἄλλοι δὲ Ἠλίαν, ἕτεροι δὲ Ἰερεμίαν ἢ ἕνα τῶν προφητῶν.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de eipan· Hoi men Iōannēn ton baptistēn, alloi de Ēlian, heteroi de Ieremian ē hena tōn prophētōn.

paragraphs.text: He saith unto them, But who say ye that I am?
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνα με λέγετε εἶναι;
paragraphs.translit: legei autois· Hymeis de tina me legete einai;

paragraphs.text: And Simon Peter answered and said, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.
paragraphs.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ Σίμων Πέτρος εἶπεν· Σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος.
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis de Simōn Petros eipen· Sy ei ho christos ho hyios tou theou tou zōntos.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus answered and said unto him, Blessed art thou, Simon Bar-jonah: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father who is in heaven.
paragraphs.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Μακάριος εἶ, Σίμων Βαριωνᾶ, ὅτι σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα οὐκ ἀπεκάλυψέν σοι ἀλλʼ ὁ πατήρ μου ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς·
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis de ho Iēsous eipen autō· Makarios ei, Simōn Bariōna, hoti sarx kai haima ouk apekalypsen soi allʼ ho patēr mou ho en tois ouranois·

paragraphs.text: And I also say unto thee, that thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.
paragraphs.original: κἀγὼ δέ σοι λέγω ὅτι σὺ εἶ Πέτρος, καὶ ἐπὶ ταύτῃ τῇ πέτρᾳ οἰκοδομήσω μου τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, καὶ πύλαι ᾅδου οὐ κατισχύσουσιν αὐτῆς·
paragraphs.translit: kagō de soi legō hoti sy ei Petros, kai epi tautē tē petra oikodomēsō mou tēn ekklēsian, kai pylai hadou ou katischysousin autēs·

paragraphs.text: I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven; and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.
paragraphs.original: δώσω σοι τὰς κλεῖδας τῆς βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν, καὶ ὃ ἐὰν δήσῃς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται δεδεμένον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, καὶ ὃ ἐὰν λύσῃς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται λελυμένον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: dōsō soi tas kleidas tēs basileias tōn ouranōn, kai ho ean dēsēs epi tēs gēs estai dedemenon en tois ouranois, kai ho ean lysēs epi tēs gēs estai lelymenon en tois ouranois.

paragraphs.text: Then charged he the disciples that they should tell no man that he was the Christ.
paragraphs.original: τότε διεστείλατο τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ εἴπωσιν ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ χριστός.
paragraphs.translit: tote diesteilato tois mathētais hina mēdeni eipōsin hoti autos estin ho christos.

paragraphs.text: From that time began Jesus to show unto his disciples, that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and the third day be raised up.
paragraphs.original: Ἀπὸ τότε ἤρξατο ὁ Ἰησοῦς δεικνύειν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ὅτι δεῖ αὐτὸν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀπελθεῖν καὶ πολλὰ παθεῖν ἀπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ ἀρχιερέων καὶ γραμματέων καὶ ἀποκτανθῆναι καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθῆναι.
paragraphs.translit: Apo tote ērxato ho Iēsous deiknyein tois mathētais autou hoti dei auton eis Hierosolyma apelthein kai polla pathein apo tōn presbyterōn kai archiereōn kai grammateōn kai apoktanthēnai kai tē tritē hēmera egerthēnai.

paragraphs.text: And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall never be unto thee.
paragraphs.original: καὶ προσλαβόμενος αὐτὸν ὁ Πέτρος ἤρξατο ἐπιτιμᾶν αὐτῷ λέγων· Ἵλεώς σοι, κύριε· οὐ μὴ ἔσται σοι τοῦτο.
paragraphs.translit: kai proslabomenos auton ho Petros ērxato epitiman autō legōn· Hileōs soi, kyrie· ou mē estai soi touto.

paragraphs.text: But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art a stumbling-block unto me: for thou mindest not the things of God, but the things of men.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ στραφεὶς εἶπεν τῷ Πέτρῳ· Ὕπαγε ὀπίσω μου, Σατανᾶ· σκάνδαλον εἶ ἐμοῦ, ὅτι οὐ φρονεῖς τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ἀλλὰ τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
paragraphs.translit: ho de strapheis eipen tō Petrō· Hypage opisō mou, Satana· skandalon ei emou, hoti ou phroneis ta tou theou alla ta tōn anthrōpōn.

paragraphs.text: Then said Jesus unto his disciples, If any man would come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
paragraphs.original: Τότε ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Εἴ τις θέλει ὀπίσω μου ἐλθεῖν, ἀπαρνησάσθω ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀράτω τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθείτω μοι.
paragraphs.translit: Tote ho Iēsous eipen tois mathētais autou· Ei tis thelei opisō mou elthein, aparnēsasthō heauton kai aratō ton stauron autou kai akoloutheitō moi.

paragraphs.text: For whosoever would save his life shall lose it: and whosoever shall lose his life for my sake shall find it.
paragraphs.original: ὃς γὰρ ἐὰν θέλῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ σῶσαι ἀπολέσει αὐτήν· ὃς δʼ ἂν ἀπολέσῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εὑρήσει αὐτήν.
paragraphs.translit: hos gar ean thelē tēn psychēn autou sōsai apolesei autēn· hos dʼ an apolesē tēn psychēn autou heneken emou heurēsei autēn.

paragraphs.text: For what shall a man be profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and forfeit his life? or what shall a man give in exchange for his life?
paragraphs.original: τί γὰρ ὠφεληθήσεται ἄνθρωπος ἐὰν τὸν κόσμον ὅλον κερδήσῃ τὴν δὲ ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ζημιωθῇ; ἢ τί δώσει ἄνθρωπος ἀντάλλαγμα τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ;
paragraphs.translit: ti gar ōphelēthēsetai anthrōpos ean ton kosmon holon kerdēsē tēn de psychēn autou zēmiōthē; ē ti dōsei anthrōpos antallagma tēs psychēs autou;

paragraphs.text: For the Son of man shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then shall he render unto every man according to his deeds.
paragraphs.original: μέλλει γὰρ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεσθαι ἐν τῇ δόξῃ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων αὐτοῦ, καὶ τότε ἀποδώσει ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὴν πρᾶξιν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: mellei gar ho hyios tou anthrōpou erchesthai en tē doxē tou patros autou meta tōn angelōn autou, kai tote apodōsei hekastō kata tēn praxin autou.

paragraphs.text: Verily I say unto you, there are some of them that stand here, who shall in no wise taste of death, till they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom.
paragraphs.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἰσίν τινες τῶν ὧδε ἑστώτων οἵτινες οὐ μὴ γεύσωνται θανάτου ἕως ἂν ἴδωσιν τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: amēn legō hymin hoti eisin tines tōn hōde hestōtōn hoitines ou mē geusōntai thanatou heōs an idōsin ton hyion tou anthrōpou erchomenon en tē basileia autou.
